title: Astrid and the Room
premise: Xanthe Ashgrove, a nonbinary property surveyor estranged from their own family, is hired to appraise Hollowmere House before its demolition. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, the house begins appraising Xanthe back — measuring their memories, their losses, their worth — and pulls them into its rooms, which rearrange like a house remembering. Xanthe discovers that in 1974 the Ashgrove family's patriarch stole a child from the household and buried the theft beneath the floorboards, and the house has been holding everyone who entered hostage to that debt ever since. To escape before the harvest moon rises, Xanthe must return what was taken: not the child's remains, but her name, restored through the found family of the house's other trapped souls. In the end, Xanthe speaks the name aloud as the moon crests, the door opens outward for the first time in fifty years, and Xanthe walks out carrying the family they never had.
about_author: Casper Okonkwo is a former building inspector turned horror writer whose debut novella won the Nightjar Prize for small-press fiction. He lives above a decommissioned funeral home, where he insists the drafts are only drafts.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe arrives at Hollowmere House to conduct a pre-demolition survey, noting its impossible measurements — rooms larger inside than out. A cold first night establishes their loneliness and habit of rationalizing noises. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking grief over their estranged family.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The excavation crew unearths a cellar door bolted shut from within; when Xanthe touches it, the hinges exhale. That night the house measures them — mirrors showing rooms they've never stood in. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination, the surveyor unable to stop taking notes.

chapters.title: Occupants
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe meets the others the house keeps: Marisol, a contractor missing since 1998, and old Teddy, who arrived in 1974 and remembers everything. They explain the rules — the house appraises, and it never finds anyone worth enough to release. Emotional beat: tentative kinship, the first flicker of found family.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: POV Teddy (1974 interwoven with present). Teddy recounts the night patriarch Edmund Ashgrove took his granddaughter Wren from the servants' quarters and sealed the truth beneath the floor. The house has demanded her return ever since. Emotional beat: guilt passed down like inheritance, and Teddy's hope that Xanthe might be different.

chapters.title: Rooms That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The house begins staging scenes from Xanthe's own past — their mother's voice behind doors, their dead brother's coat on a hook — testing whether Xanthe will trade memories for passage. Xanthe refuses and the corridors punish them. Emotional beat: identity under siege, choosing selfhood over comfort.

chapters.title: The Harvest Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Marisol deciphers the ledger hidden in the walls: every occupant the house has 'appraised' and kept, each entry ending in a red line. She realizes the harvest moon is six days away and the house grows hungrier as it nears. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve; Marisol stops being a victim and becomes a strategist.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Following Teddy's directions, Xanthe digs beneath the original floorboards and finds Wren's belongings — a tin whistle, a christening record bearing her full name: Wren Amarantha Ashgrove. The house screams through the pipes. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; Xanthe understands the debt is theirs to pay.

chapters.title: The House Objects
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. As Xanthe prepares the rite of return, the house turns hostile — walls contracting, doors vanishing, Teddy taken by the corridor as collateral. Marisol holds the stairwell while Xanthe climbs toward the sealed door. Emotional beat: sacrifice and fury; the found family fighting for one another.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Under the rising moon, Xanthe presses their palm to the inside-sealed door and speaks Wren's name aloud, returning what was taken — the theft, the silence, the erasure. The bolts turn themselves. The house, appraising Xanthe one final time, finds them worth letting go. Emotional beat: catharsis; naming as restitution.

chapters.title: Deed and Title
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Dawn. Xanthe, Marisol, and freed Teddy walk out as the house settles into ordinary ruin. Xanthe files a final appraisal listing Wren Amarantha Ashgrove as the true owner, then keeps the found family close instead of walking away. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — inheritance redefined as belonging chosen, not blood.
